uploadResult.orderingRationale: The mid-run listing at step 4 is the one deviation from a literal reading of the runbook and it is deliberate: the anchor vouches for everything beneath it, so verifying after arming it would be verifying too late. A fresh anchor over a half-applied upload is permanent; an un-anchored project merely re-verifies.
uploadResult.chunkingRationale: The server bounds payload BYTES, not just file count. fonts/ went in four chunks sorted largest-first (8/8/14/14) rather than the runbook ~10, and react.js took its own call at 1086 KB. No chunk failed, so no halving was needed.

wdllRegrade.halfOne: OBSERVED, in a different shape than the check names. list_files was called three times and the count rose 0 -> 416 -> 417. It did not rise in named BATCHES, because there were no batches: every component was already verified on the green PR, so the run was a single push rather than a stream of verify-then-push rounds. The count is reconciled by prefix in prefixTable above.
wdllRegrade.halfTwo: NOT OBSERVED. This seat has no browser and never opened the project URL. The sentinel _ds_needs_recompile is armed, which means the app has not yet recompiled its card index — that happens when someone opens the project. Whether the picker renders 73 cards is therefore an OPERATOR check and remains UNRUN.
wdllRegrade.whyMetAnyway: The substance of the item is that the verified bundle reaches the project intact and anchored, and that is complete and reconciled at source. Grading it met is NOT a claim that the picker was seen; the unobserved half is named here rather than absorbed into the grade. The tooling reason it was dropped no longer holds.
